intro.title: Test Error Boundary
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a test for an Error Boundary component in React. You will learn how to simulate errors in a child component to verify that your Error Boundary catches and displays a fallback UI as expected. The core programming concept involves using React's Error Boundary lifecycle methods and writing unit tests with a testing library like React Testing Library. You will work with constructs such as try-catch simulation, mocking errors, and assertions to ensure the Error Boundary functions correctly. This hands-on practice will help you understand how to make your React applications more robust by testing error handling.
intro.usecase: Error boundaries are essential in production React applications where components can fail unexpectedly. In a financial dashboard, an error boundary prevents a single faulty stock chart from crashing the entire dashboard, allowing users to continue viewing other widgets. In an e-commerce product listing, if one product card fails to load due to malformed data, error boundaries ensure the rest of the products remain visible while showing a fallback UI for the problematic item. Testing these boundaries ensures your application gracefully handles failures without disrupting the user experience.
